references.text: Deals with impurity from touching a dead animal or carrion, which makes the person unclean.
Describes how touching dead animals makes a person unclean until evening, the same principle as in verse 39.
Continuation of the law concerning dead animals, where eating or carrying the carcass requires washing and results in impurity until evening.
Repeats the law on impurity for one who eats a dead animal or a torn animal, and the requirement for cleansing.
Prohibits priests from eating dead animals, linked to the impurity laws in chapter 11.
Elaborates on the laws regarding impurity from touching dead bodies and the duration of the impurity.
Forbids eating dead animals and permits giving them to foreigners, related to the purity laws.
Ezekiel declares that he has never eaten a dead animal or torn meat, a reference to the purity laws in Leviticus.
Priests shall not eat dead or torn animals, linked to the law of impurity.
